standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A is elementary in M when the two structures satisfy the same formulas with parameters in A.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis and part of the conclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generated subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: The subsystem generated by A is the closure of A under the partial operation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the subsystem shown to be elementary.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ordering extending a given one
standard_prerequisites.statement: An HF-ordering of the generated subsystem can be chosen so that its closure of A is A itself.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the extra information the proof provides.

core_obligations: Decompose the generated subsystem into its finite stages and use the hypothesis on A to show that each stage stays inside A's closure and remains elementary (source line 911).
Choose an HF-ordering of the generated subsystem whose closure of A is A, which also gives the isomorphism, rather than invoking the closure lemma (source line 911).

proof_roadmap.step: Stage by stage, show the generated subsystem is elementary.
Choose the ordering with the prescribed closure.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 909-910: if A is an elementary subsystem of an unconfined system then the subsystem generated by A is also elementary, and moreover there is an HF-ordering of it whose closure of A is A. The proof (source lines 911-912) does not take the short route through the closure lemma, and the author says so explicitly; instead it decomposes the generated subsystem into finite stages and uses the elementarity of A at each stage, which is what also produces the isomorphism and hence the ordering with the prescribed closure. The statement records the elementarity and the existence of the ordering, and neither the stage decomposition nor the reason for avoiding the shorter argument.
